entries.name: Boyd Payton

expected.charges: Conspiracy to dynamite a Carolina Power & Light Company electrical substation and to destroy two textile-mill buildings.
expected.sentence:
Six to ten years in prison (1960); commuted July 4, 1961; full pardon December 31, 1964.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted in 1960 in North Carolina superior court and sentenced to six to ten years. Governor Terry Sanford commuted the sentences on July 4, 1961 and granted Payton a full pardon on December 31, 1964.

Charges as recorded: Conspiracy to dynamite a Carolina Power & Light Company electrical substation and to destroy two textile-mill buildings during the 1958–59 Harriet-Henderson Cotton Mills strike — a charge widely regarded as a frame-up of the union's leadership (Payton said the only evidence against him was a phone call in which he warned a caller that the line was bugged). Charged with seven others in June 1959.

updates.sentence:

entries.rationale: Contemporary AP report, Friday November 4, explicitly reports Thursday surrender and imprisonment and names Payton. Refine November 1960 to November 3; July 1959 conviction already confirmed by the report. Release remains August 1961 month.

entries.name: Ammon Hennacy

expected.charges: Trespass during Omaha Action against the Mead, Nebraska missile base.
expected.sentence: Served a six-month sentence at Sandstone Federal Prison for the 1959 anti-nuclear protest. Exact custody endpoints are not entered.

updates.sentence: Arrested and sentenced August 24, 1959 to six months and a $500 fine, with custody beginning immediately. Released in January 1960. Dorothy Day announced January 20 in advance; a later biography gives January 21. The exact discharge day remains unresolved, and the six-month sentence is not recorded as six months actually served.

entries.rationale: Eyewitness September 1959 Catholic Worker report dates arrest, same-day sentence and immediate custody August 24. January 20 was an advance release announcement; biography says January 21, while February 1960 diary confirms he was free by late January. Preserve supported month, remove sentence-as-time-served override.
